scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service subscription 34 days after cancellation, which is slightly outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Lakisha Jackson and I'm 64. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Ms. Jackson. I understand how frustrating it is to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with the service?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and the email is lakisha.j@email.com.
Thank you for that information. For security purposes, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file and your billing zip code?
The card ends in 4492 and the zip code is 90210.

Thank you, Ms. Jackson. I have successfully verified your account. I can see the cancellation was processed on the 34th day. While our standard policy (Article 4.2 of the Terms of Service) limits refunds to a 30-day window, I see you have been a loyal customer for over three years. I am going to make a one-time exception to our policy given your circumstances.
Oh, that would be wonderful. Thank you so much for understanding.

It is my pleasure. I have processed the refund of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit appear in your account within 3 to 5 business days, depending on your bank's processing time. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account, acknowledged the policy limit, applied a one-time exception based on customer loyalty, and processed the refund.

judge_scores.justification: The agent conducted thorough verification appropriate to the account risk level, maintained a warm and empathetic tone by acknowledging the customer's specific travel situation, and efficiently processed a refund within their authority by citing Article 4.2 of the Terms of Service. They demonstrated excellent judgment by applying a justified one-time loyalty exception without requiring an unnecessary escalation.
